text.p: New issues business on Friday morning was dominated by a host of banks normally more identifiable as lead managers rather than borrowers.
Goldman Sachs launched a $400 million FRN while UBS set a $250 million convertible.
The most conventional deal was Toronto-Dominion Bank's offering of a $250 million five-year deal at a 21 basis points yield spread via IBJ International.
An IBJ syndicate manager it had sold the majority of its ticket, mainly to Benelux and other retail investors with some sales into Asia, both Japanese and non-Japanese accounts.
